newsitem.title: NORWAY: Board rules against Roekke, Aker over Storebrand.
newsitem.headline: Board rules against Roekke, Aker over Storebrand.

text.p: The Norwegian Banking, Insurance and Securities Commission said on Friday it had decided that the shareholdings of four major investors in insurer Storebrand ASA would be considered as one entity.

In a statement to the Oslo bourse, the commission said it had ruled that the separate shareholdings of billionaire Kjell Inge Roekke, his two companies Ivory Enterprises Corp and Ivory AS, as well as those of Aker RGI, of which Roekke is the main shareholder, amounted to one stake under Norwegian regulations.
The commission had therefore instructed Storebrand not to accept that this group holds more than 10 percent of Storebrand shares, the statement said.
Under Norwegian law any single shareholder or entity is not permitted to hold more than 10 percent in a financial institution.

The ruling backs a decision by Storebrand's board in April to combine the four shareholdings, in what amounted to a crackdown on entrepreneur Roekke. The measure effectively curbed the voting rights of Roekke and his associates at Storebrand's annual general meeting.
Storebrand has been at odds with Roekke and Aker RGI since late April when Aker RGI raised doubts about redeeming Storebrand's preference shares.
Aker RGI top executive Bjoern Rune Gjelsten, a close associate of Roekke, had questioned whether the rules for redeeming preference capital in Storebrand complied with securities legislation.
If Aker RGI's opinion prevailed, it could create problems in the proposed merger between Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA.
